newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: BOK steps in to cap won's rise vs dollar - dealers.
newsitem.headline: BOK steps in to cap won's rise vs dollar - dealers.

text.p: The central bank of Korea intervened in the interbank market in late afternoon on Friday to slow the won's rise against the dollar, dealers said.
The central bank denied it intervened. Dealers said the central bank stepped in after the won jumped to an intraday high of 819.50. The won soon fell back to the 822 level.
"The central bank probably didn't like the dollar falling so sharply so quickly," said a dealer. The won opened at 824.40.
Traders said there was no buying of dollars as the market sentiment turned sour towards the U.S. unit. Export deals and dollar selling by foreign banks depressed the mood, they said.
But the won's sudden rise surprised the market after its apparent weakness early this week. The won reached an all-time low of 830.00 on Monday. -- Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5643
